# Copper Scroll Column 6 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Copper Scroll Column 6 (treasure locations 21-25) where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 6:1 — underground passage/tunnel

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the underground passage which is on the south side" |
| LOGOS | "the underground passage on the southern side" |
| PNEUMA | "the tunnel running south" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS phrasing — drops the relative "which is" for economy while keeping "underground passage."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 6:3-4 — gold of tribute / gold from tribute / tribute gold

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "gold of tribute and sixty talents of gold" |
| LOGOS | "gold from tribute amounting to sixty talents" |
| PNEUMA | "tribute gold — sixty talents of gold in all" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET's "gold of tribute" as most literal for the construct chain. The "and" before sixty talents preserved as in the Hebrew.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 6:5 — cave of the pillar which has two openings / two-mouthed cave

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the cave of the pillar which has two openings" |
| LOGOS | "the cave of the pillar with two openings" |
| PNEUMA | "the two-mouthed cave by the pillar" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's compact form "the cave of the pillar with two openings." PNEUMA's "two-mouthed" is vivid but not standard.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 6:7-8 — buried/depth phrasing + scroll description

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "buried three cubits — there is a pitcher; in it, one scroll" |
| LOGOS | "buried three cubits deep — there is a pitcher; within it, one scroll" |
| PNEUMA | "three cubits down — a pitcher sits there; inside it, a single scroll" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET's rendering as most faithful. "Buried three cubits" without additional words matches the terse Hebrew. "One scroll" is literal for sefer echad.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 6:9 — near the above/adjacent/neighboring

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the cave near the above" |
| LOGOS | "the cave adjacent to the above" |
| PNEUMA | "the neighboring cave" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET's "near the above" as the most literal rendering of the Hebrew directional reference.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 6:12 — uncoined silver / raw uncoined silver

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "uncoined silver" |
| LOGOS | "uncoined silver" |
| PNEUMA | "raw, uncoined silver" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "uncoined silver" per EMET/LOGOS. PNEUMA's "raw" is redundant with "uncoined."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 6:14 — sheepcote/sheepfold/sheep pen

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the sheepcote" — archaic English for dir |
| LOGOS | "the sheepfold" — standard |
| PNEUMA | "the sheep pen" — modern |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's "sheepfold" as the standard English rendering — less archaic than "sheepcote," more precise than "sheep pen."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

*Total disagreements in Column 6: 7*
